long_biography.plain_text:
A six-month spell at sea while studying engineering gave Atlas Maritime founder Leon Patitsas a direct view of the isolation and demands faced by merchant crews. He later paired his Tufts engineering degree with a master's from MIT, then worked for a Swiss bank in New York investing institutional assets in hedge funds.

As chief executive, Patitsas applies that financial grounding to shipping cycles. Atlas buys vessels at distressed prices, places them on medium- or long-term contracts, uses operating cash flow to repay debt and sells when markets strengthen. He has also formed joint ventures with private-equity and asset-management partners across several financial centres, making capital discipline and market timing central to the company's operating model.
